body.statement: A language lies in \(\Sigma _2^{\mathrm P}\) if and only if membership has an \(\exists x\,\forall z\) characterization by a deterministic polynomial-time predicate, with both quantified strings of polynomial length.

source.locator: Section 2, displayed quantified-verifier definition of the polynomial hierarchy on pages 2--3
source.verbatim_statement: A language L is contained in Sigma_k^p iff there exists some polynomial-time computable function V (verifier), and m_1, m_2, ..., m_k = poly(|w|) such that for all w: w in L iff exists y_1 forall y_2 ... Q y_k: V(w,y_1,y_2,...,y_k)=1.

upstream.citation: Larry J. Stockmeyer. The polynomial-time hierarchy. Theoretical Computer Science 3(1):1--22, 1976. DOI: 10.1016/0304-3975(76)90061-X.
upstream.locator: Definition of the polynomial hierarchy by alternating polynomially bounded quantifiers

attestation.note: Verified against Grüne and Wulf, The Complexity of Blocking All Solutions, arXiv:2502.05348v1, Section 2, p. 4 of the arXiv PDF (published pagination p. 4); specialization k=2 gives the cited exists-forall characterization. Open author-posted arXiv copy retrieved 2026-09-16.
